title: Onprem triage & smokecheck playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working playbook is a living triage and smoke-test checklist for Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments. It focuses on the most common install and runtime failure modes we see during customer installs and upgrades, and provides quick verification commands, expected outputs, and short remediation steps. Target audience: site reliability, solutions engineering, and field install engineers.

Quick orientation (read first):
- Run the basic smoke checklist before escalating. Many issues are environmental (DNS, MTU, kernel drivers) and are often solved by a few diagnostic commands.
- When in doubt, collect the diagnostics bundle (diagnostics.sh) and attach to JIRA/Slack case.
- This doc intentionally favors short pragmatic commands and known good fixes; it is not a full runbook for every component.

Common failure categories we see:
1) Networking - DNS, routes, MTU, firewall rules
2) K8s node join / Kubelet problems
3) Container runtime / cgroup / GPU driver mismatches
4) Certs / mTLS / KMS connectivity failures
5) Storage mounts (NFS/iSCSI) and PV/PVC binding problems
6) Terraform state and module drift during bootstrap
7) App-level: agent not connecting, API 5xx, caches degraded

Minimum reproducible checklist (run in sequence) - 8 minutes:
1) Node & system health (30s):
- uname -a  # confirm kernel is supported
- uptime; free -m; df -h /opt/redwood
- systemctl is-active kubelet || journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager
Expected: kubelet running, reasonable memory free, /opt/redwood not full (>20% free recommended).

2) Kubernetes overview (1m):
- kubectl get nodes -o wide
- kubectl get pods -A --field-selector=status.phase!=Running
Expected: control plane and worker nodes Ready, no CrashLoopBackOff in core namespaces. If master/controlplane not ready, collect API server logs: kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/kube-apiserver.

3) Container runtime checks (1m):
- crictl ps -a || docker ps -a
- crictl runtimeconfig || docker info | head -n 20
- check GPU: nvidia-smi (if GPU node)
Expected: container runtime responsive. If crictl fails, check /var/log/syslog and journalctl -u containerd. Common fix: restart container runtime and kubelet: sudo systemctl restart containerd kubelet; wait 30s.

4) Networking checks (1m):
- ip route; ip -s link show
- dig +short api.redwood.local @10.0.0.2 (replace DNS)
- curl -sS --connect-timeout 3 http://10.0.0.1:8080/healthz
Expected: DNS resolves, no packet drops on host NICs, health endpoints reachable. If DNS fails, check /etc/resolv.conf and kube-dns/coredns pods. For MTU issues (VPN overlays) compare host MTU to pod overlay MTU.

5) Storage / PV checks (45s):
- kubectl get pv,pvc -o wide
- ls -la /mnt/redwood-storage (host path or mountpoint)
Expected: PVs bound, PVCs claim status Bound. If stuck Pending, check StorageClass and provisioner logs. For NFS: showmount -e nfs-server-host. If mount failing, ensure nfs-common installed and NFS server allows client subnet.

6) App-level smoke checks (2m):
- curl -sS http://<ingress-ip>/v1/health | jq .status
- kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/redwood-agent -c agent --tail=200
Expected: health endpoint returns "ok" and recent logs show successful connection to control plane/registry. Common errors: 401/403 (credential issues) — verify KMS keys or service account tokens.

Quick triage templates (how to interpret common outputs):
- CrashLoopBackOff with ExitCode 137: OOM. Check container memory limits and node memory. Increase limits or tune batching.
- ImagePullBackOff: registry auth or ephemeral network DNS. Try docker pull manually and inspect image repo credentials.
- ETCD auth errors after upgrade: clock skew. Check ntp/chrony service on all control plane nodes.

Terraform module notes (bootstrap & drift checks):
- Always run terraform init && terraform validate in the module root. Keep backend lock (S3 with DynamoDB or remote backend) to avoid parallel applies.
- Recommended variables to pin in private deployments: aws_region (or cloud_region), instance_profile, allowed_cidrs, k8s_version, docker_image_tag (pin exact digest for critical components).
- Outputs to include in module: control_plane_endpoint, kubeconfig_blob (S3 path), cluster_ca_fingerprint. These reduce ad-hoc discovery during installs.
- Drift detection: terraform plan -var-file=secrets.tfvars. If resources already created by other tooling, import them into state using terraform import to avoid replace.
- Workspaces: use a workspace per customer environment (dev/stage/prod). For upgrades, create a staging workspace referencing the same module and run plan there first.

Typical Terraform failure patterns and quick remedies:
- Conflicting security group rules: compare remote state + cloud console. Modify rules via terraform or import cloud-managed resources.
- Provider version mismatch after an upgrade: pin provider versions in providers.tf. If state is incompatible, use provider aliasing as interim mitigation.
- Backend lock errors: ensure DynamoDB (or equivalent) table exists and IAM credentials used by CI have dynamo:LockTable permissions.

Upgrade plan (short checklist for minor/patch upgrades):
1) Pre-upgrade (day before):
- Run full smoke suite and create backup snapshot of DBs and S3-compatible object stores.
- Export current terraform state to a timestamped location.
- Check release notes for breaking changes (schema migrations, k8s API removals).

2) Canary phase (preferred):
- Select 1-2 worker nodes as canary. Drain a canary node and apply upgrade to pods running there (use nodeSelector or cordon/drain/helm upgrade with nodeAffinity). Observe 30-60 minutes for errors.

3) Rolling update:
- Use kubectl rollout status and watch metrics (errors, latency). Typical safe window: 2x expected pod restart time.
- For DB-backed components, ensure migrations are run in read-only compatible mode or use a migration job with leader-election.

4) Post-upgrade verification:
- Run smoke checklist. Confirm metrics, traces, and logs for error spikes.
- If rollback required, use helm rollback or restore from snapshot; for terraform-level issues, run terraform apply with previous module version.

Diagnostic commands & artifacts to collect (one-liner bundle):
- sudo /opt/redwood/tools/collect-diagnostics.sh --out /tmp/redwood-diag.tar.gz
- Manually include: /var/log/redwood/*.log, /var/log/syslog, journalctl -u kubelet -n 500, kubectl get all -A -o wide, helm list -A, terraform show -json > /tmp/tfstate.json

Specific remediation snippets (copy/paste friendly):
- Restart agent and stream logs: sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent && sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent -f -n 200
- Repair kubelet credential expiry: sudo systemctl restart kubelet && kubectl get nodes && kubectl describe node <node-name> to surface kubelet auth errors.
- Force reclaim PV stuck in Terminating: kubectl patch pv <pv-name> -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":null}}' --type=merge

Security & KMS/HSM common problems:
- Symptom: 401 from encryption service, logs show TLS handshake failed.
- Quick checks: openssl s_client -connect kms-host:443 -servername kms-host and verify presented cert CN matches expected. Ensure vault/KMS IAM roles or service accounts are bound and secrets are present in /etc/redwood/creds.
- If HSM integrated: confirm PKCS11 module path and permissions; misconfigured pkcs11 driver will cause key load failures at agent startup.

When to escalate to SRE or Eng applied-ml:
- Reproducible CrashLoopBackOff across >25% of nodes after restart or upgrade.
- Persistent API 500s after rollback attempts.
- Data corruption detected in persistent stores or failed DB migrations.

Notes & gotchas from field installs (lessons learned):
- MTU mismatches between customer VPN and overlay network cause intermittent gRPC failures; recommend verifying MTU end-to-end and setting overlay mtu in CNI.
- Customers often have restrictive egress policies. Document the exact egress CIDRs and ports required: 443 (control plane), 123 (ntp), 5671 (if AMQP used), 2181 (zookeeper) etc.
- Opaque errors during upgrade are frequently caused by a single misconfigured cloud resource (security groups, route table). Start the triage with cloud console checks when install steps fail.

Open action items (for this doc):
- Add a short script to run the 8-minute checklist automatically and produce a one-page summary.
- Add a mapping matrix of common error log snippets -> Jira KB article for quick copy/paste.

Slack escalation shortcuts (internal):
- #private-deployments-escalate (SRE on-call P1), include diag bundle link and terraform plan output.
- @oncall-eng (pager schedule) for time-sensitive rollbacks.

Appendix: quick expected outputs (cheat-sheet)
- kubectl get nodes: all Ready
- curl /v1/health: {"status":"ok"}
- docker info: Server Version: >= 20.10 or containerd runtime present

If you hit something not in this doc, collect the diagnostics bundle and ping the channel with the bundle link and the exact command sequence that caused the failure.

End of playbook (draft) — Lena 2024-09 (please edit inline; this should be iterative and kept under the private-deployments directory).
